During 5.3, VRChat instituted a "muted first" policy where everyone was muted and you had to opt-in to hear them. That was a bad idea, and how the safety and trust system is currently implemented is bad too. VRChat needs to hire an actual social scientist for these non-technical aspects to prevent such anti-social situations in the future.

I do not have any additional suggestion or comment because I'm not a social scientist and this should be designed and instituted by experts in their field, not computer scientists and users.

@{58c6da1b23f8d63e1401d381|full_name}: I think users should have some say in it, as they're the ones who use and are affected by the systems in place.
Otherwise I totally agree, they need someone with understandings of social dynamics on their team.

@{58c6da1b23f8d63e1401d381|full_name}: I do somewhat agree with this up until the part about users. It it wasnt for users, the muted first policy would still be a thing. The users of the product or service know what they want, and when they are displeased, we have the full right to voice our opinions. The point of VRChat is to cater to its users and provide features that they think will add to the experience of the platform in a positive way. If they fail to do this, they will lose users. The point of canny is for us to voice these things so that does not happen.

@{598ac3b7ae70f9414a0953ce|full_name}: Saying "NO! BAD!" on Canny is all the users can do, and it's probably for the best. I think we are better off just saying "NO! BAD!" vs. negotiation on the execution of a user facing system which is fundamentally broken. 

Without a social scientist on the team, it will be extremely challenging for this stretched dev team to find a "good" way to incorporate this system which fails to take into account the many ways colors, titles, and the use of the "invisible hand" to progress in "rank" are used to keep other people down throughout history and even currently. Caste systems, religion, and the fear of the "other" in general is a bad initial precedent to set, and this rapidly spirals down that rabbit hole.

@{5a08a282aa8343184dd6dcfa|full_name}: Everyone already has preconceived notions of other users the instant they see them, then they change from the first word (if any), and then change again.

The visible ranks create more of these in a way the user has very little control over.

There have been people refusing to talk to users with veteran rank purely because of that rank.
Social divisions created where there were none.

@{5a08a282aa8343184dd6dcfa|full_name}: Given how you can customise who you can hear with the ranks system, if you are a veteran user and the people you meet have made it so users and veterans are mute to them, you are effectively blocked from that social interaction, which is something that cannot be controlled by the user.

Given how there has been discrimination against veteran users for  reasons that are probably linked to them not having it, this could be an issue that could damage the social presence of VRChat.

If particles and shaders are such a problem that they need to be blocked for some users, then a simple solution would be to just block them via an option. This feature feels overly engineered and promotes social hierarchy, and when that becomes a focus (because even though the titles and name tag colours do not have any meaning to them, the user base will assign some to them), it might split the community again like around December of 2017.

I would agree that a different way of implementing this feature would be greatly appreciated.

Additionally, this system is not working in a way that makes any sense when the first part of the description for Veteran is "…have been citizens of VRChat for a very long time" and people very active since 2016 or earlier don't have that rank. This is very dismissive of a lot of people who have been active for a very long time.

It shouldn't be so prominent if the descriptions don't even line up with reality. There are active users who have contributed a lot socially to this game via organizing events and being great people that don't have this rank. While people who joined in 2018 do.

The whole thing is forcing judgment and a resulting label upon users that other users will then use to make assumptions about them.

>People can make an assumption based on everything they see or hear first in real life and VR. -- Lycon

This label is not something people are presenting by choice. It is not their choice of avatar, how polite they speak, or the content they are sharing with you at the moment. It is a label arbitrarily and mysteriously applied to them by the aristocracy that is the VRChat Development team.

I feel like the content creation signals being mixed into this system is a huge flaw after seeing how ranks have been distributed. _Espcially when the description starts with "…have been citizens of VRChat for a *very long time*."

I completely agree that rank should not be a visible thing on nameplates. Dont get me wrong the colors are pretty but this is exactly something Altspace messed up that caused a massive jealousy fueled class war of sorts in the community. Would prefer we avoid that here.

It's alarming to know that players are finding ways to abuse this system such as the group block in efforts to de-rank like you mentioned. While the blame can't be completely rested on the company for this petty behaviour, they should really consult someone with a high degree of knowledge on inter-human social interactions before implementing something like this that's so out in the open.

I agree that the presentation of this system could definitely use some alterations.
Caste system must go.
@{5964e9a60248e65ef59d76be|full_name}: +1

details:
The Rank system is obviously designed as a way to allow users to block certain aspects of other users to help better their experience when playing. This is a good idea in theory, and makes a lot of sense. But the way the system is presented gives it the feeling of a social hierarchy. A user’s rank is not something that should be visible via the nameplate color, and should be a small section of a user’s details page. Making it visible via the name plate color helps users to create assumptions about the user they may be thinking of talking to before they even say a word. And in an app where being social is everything, first impressions are a massive deal. I’m already seeing examples of groups of users blocking someone all at once in an attempt to de-rank them, or rooms of lower ranked users all just agreeing to kick the one veteran ranked user in the room out of jealousy. I feel like if I stopped there the response would be “well just hide your rank as user”. The issue with being able to hide your rank as user now is that the User rank has just sort of become the rank you see and automatically go “ok so that person is hiding their rank”. I have seem more users hiding their rank under the User tag, than actual users. This is making people unsure when talking to people under the user rank. Even between friends there is a lot of teasing about who has what rank. And while it is just teasing, it does help prove to me that the idea of this social hierarchy is even at the forefront of everyone’s minds, even when with friends. So to sum it up, I think that if the company wants to go this direction with this security feature, then by all means. But please alter the presentation, as right now it’s a security feature presented like a social status feature, which is really really miss communicating its purpose.

if you have not yet heard of this system, you can read up on it here: https://medium.com/@vrchat/vrchat-safety-and-trust-system-4073f05ab602
title: (Build 632) Change the way Ranks are Presented
